findings.evidence: relpath_join ends `| sort` with no locale pinned, and the three EXPECTED_*_SET constants are written in C-collation order (uppercase block before the lowercase docs/al-* block; .claude/** before CLAUDE.md before docs/**). The set pins compare the two blobs by string equality, so the comparison is order-SENSITIVE and the order is locale-dependent. MEASURED: (a) `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=$PWD bash <spec>` -> exit 1, 185 passed / 2 FAILED: 1S.2b and 1S.10b. (b) `LC_ALL=C ...` -> exit 0, 187/0. (c) ambient (LANG=C.UTF-8, this session) -> exit 0, 187/0, identical across two runs. Collation confirmed to differ on this machine: `LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8 sort` places docs/al-2026-* BEFORE docs/ARCHITECTURE.md; LC_ALL=C and POSIX place it after. THE SPURIOUS FAILURE IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE REAL ATTACK: my independent reproduction of the R6-F3 drop-plus-add (discover_docs_md mutated to drop docs/HOOKS.md and add .claude/rubrics/default.md) also yields exit 1, 185 passed / 2 failed, THE SAME TWO ASSERTIONS. The locale diff prints 10 '-' lines and 10 '+' lines, i.e. it reads as twenty file movements, and one of the '-' lines is '-docs/HOOKS.md' -- the exact file R6-F3 cited as its silently-dropped example. HOUSE CONVENTION DEVIATED FROM: `LC_ALL=C sort` is used for sorted-set comparisons in at least 14 sibling L1 specs (packaging-parity.test.sh:323/329/334, mcp-deps.test.sh:298/300/307/314, lessons.test.sh:562-573, impact-report.test.sh:672, gate-claim-honesty.test.sh:1366/1441), and change-set-undeterminable.test.sh:158 ASSERTS the production tracker pins it (tracker_lines=$(LC_ALL=C sort -u ...)). FIX PROVEN: changing that one `sort` to `LC_ALL=C sort` gives 187/0 under en_US.UTF-8, C AND fr_FR.UTF-8, and the drop-plus-add attack still fails exactly 1S.2b/1S.10b under en_US.UTF-8 (185/2). One word, one site, assertion count unchanged.
findings.description: The R6-F3 fix defeats its own stated purpose in a common environment. R6-F3's goal was that the failure NAME which path appeared or disappeared instead of only that a number moved; under any UTF-8 collating locale it names twenty phantom movements, including the very file the finding was about. Worse, the helper prints its own remediation recipe -- 'paste the "+ ..." line(s) above into this pin's EXPECTED_*_SET constant ... and drop any "- ..." line(s)' -- so a maintainer on a default macOS Terminal (LANG=en_US.UTF-8) or a UTF-8-collating Linux desktop who follows the spec's OWN printed instruction rewrites the pinned constant into their locale's order, breaking it for everyone on C collation and 'resolving' it by transcription rather than investigation. That is precisely the outcome the round-7 brief named as worse than no pin. It is a REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THIS ROUND: before R6-F3 these categories were pinned by COUNT, which is locale-independent (bash array lengths), so this spec carried no locale-dependent assertion until now. It is also INVISIBLE TO THE UPCOMING FOUR-TIER RUN, which inherits this session's LANG=C.UTF-8 and will report 187/0 -- so it ships green. Finally, accepting it would be internally inconsistent with what this same round just did: R6-F4 removed 'proof that' from BANNED_CLAIM_PATTERN on the express reasoning that 'a false-positive channel that pressures maintainers into rewording honest prose to go green is a real cost'. A set pin that pressures maintainers into rewriting or deleting the pin to go green is the same cost, in the same round, in the same file. NOT ASKED FOR: any change to the pinned CONTENT, to the discovery functions, or to the assertion count -- 187 stays 187.

findings.evidence: Two Section-1 banners state a scope wider than Section 1's assertions. :512 (comment) 'zero banned-claim hits across every shipped copy' -- Section 1 scans 8 qa-gate.sh + 8 verify-before-stop.sh copies; review-check.sh also ships 8 copies (measured: 8 copies, 1 unique sha256) which only 1S.0/1S.1 cover. :515 (RUNTIME banner, printed in every run) '1. SOURCE SCAN: no disguised-or-plain tamper-evidence claim ships' -- 'ships' is a claim about the world whose scope is not recoverable from the sentence at all. WHY THIS IS LOW AND NOT THE SIXTH R6-F1 INSTANCE, stated so round 8 does not re-open it: (1) nothing is left unscanned as a consequence -- review-check.sh's 8 copies ARE scanned in the same file at 1S.1, and the Sections list at :171-178 names it explicitly, so a misled reader is wrong about WHICH section covers it and right that the file covers it; contrast R6-F1, where 110 declared rows were scanned NOWHERE. (2) The proposition at :515 is TRUE and I verified it independently: a whole-tree sweep of 11,026 files with the shipped, extracted normalize_claim_text/banned_claim_count/BANNED_CLAIM_PATTERN found 17 survivor files, every one either in the deliberate OUT list (.beads/**, .claude/.qa-tracking/**, docs/reviews/**, CHANGELOG.md:2882 released entry, LESSONS.md:246), this spec quoting itself (26 hits), or run-tests.sh:592-597, whose text is a NEGATED, historical statement ('record cannot be tamper-evident'). Zero illegitimate hits tree-wide. (3) Section 1 is labelled DIAGNOSTIC, not load-bearing, at :80-87 and :163; the load-bearing controls are 2P/2Q/3.1/Section 4. So these are over-broad section titles over a true proposition, not false coverage claims -- materially weaker than R5-F1 (false against a known in-file counterexample) and R6-F1 (false against the repo's own manifest oracle). Every other totality-word hit I swept classifies as legitimate: :107, :137, :630, :632 (past-tense descriptions of the historical false claim), :135 and :1029 (explicitly NEGATED claims), :1460 ('THIS IS NOT THE FULL CONTRIBUTOR SET', the R5-F1 fix), :159/:706 ('the fuller argument'), :1320/:1778 ('the full argument'/'full reasoning' cross-references), :1043 ('the ENTIRE operator-facing surface' -- scoped to the defined union, contrasting the per-category assertions above it).
findings.description: RECORDED AS EXPLICITLY CLEARED-WITH-A-CAVEAT rather than sat on, because the operator's ruling was that after this round there should be nothing of this sentence-shape left to find. My judgment: :512 and :515 are NOT the sixth instance of the R5-F1/R6-F1 defect -- that defect is a claim of coverage that is FALSE and licenses a maintainer to stop looking at something genuinely unscanned, and neither of these is false nor leaves anything unscanned. They are, however, of the same SHAPE, they are the highest-visibility remnant of it (:515 prints on every run), and they cost one word each to end permanently. Since the file must be reopened for R7-F1 anyway, fixing them there is free. SUGGESTED, not required: scope :512 to the two scripts it actually scans (e.g. 'across all 8 copies of each of the two scripts scanned here', which is what the Sections list at :161-163 already says correctly), and scope :515 the same way (e.g. '1. SOURCE SCAN: no tamper-evidence claim in the two scripts scanned here'). Below risk_threshold=high; does not gate. If the specialist declines, that is a legitimate outcome -- this artifact is the record that the question was asked and answered, so round 8 need not re-derive it.
